thought: The blocked suffix is caused by xarm6 being failed and SAFE_1 requiring LG to be placed at the assembly station before ur5e can continue MCP place_approach. The key missing world-state uncertainty was LG's actual pose after the failed place_insert. That pose is already grounded in the session observation store: LG at (0.0, 0.2, 1.035). Resource states are also grounded: xarm6 is failed, open, not holding LG; ur5e is holding MCP and is not yet in the assembly destination area. With LG pose now known, the affected part is localized and available for recovery planning. No additional observation type is exposed beyond part_pose, and requesting LG pose again would duplicate an existing observation.
grounded_facts: xarm6@localhost is in failed state and cannot satisfy its nominal move_home continuation condition.
xarm6@localhost is not holding any part and its gripper is open.
LG is not in a gripper and has an observed pose from the session store at approximately (0.0, 0.2, 1.035).
LG is misplaced rather than assembled at assembly_board-v1, which is the reason SAFE_1 blocks REQ_1_T3.
ur5e@localhost is currently holding MCP with gripper closed.
REQ_1_T3 and REQ_1_T4 remain pending, but REQ_1_T3 is safety-blocked until LG is placed first.
SAFE_2 remains relevant because ur5e and xarm6 must not both occupy the assembly destination area simultaneously; xarm6 is failed and not reported at the assembly destination area.
recovery_implications: Recovery planning can be synthesized around the grounded LG pose instead of requiring further search/observation.
Because xarm6 has failed and released LG, recovery must reroute completion of REQ_2 away from the failed suffix and use an available capable resource/path.
ur5e cannot proceed with MCP place_approach until a recovery sequence satisfies SAFE_1 by placing LG at assembly_board-v1 first.
No additional observation request is needed before generating a recovery event sequence.
